item.text: I can use `perl` for the automation, so I’m testing a few sign-edge cases before I lock the formatter. Negative zero handling is worth checking because C++ streams preserve it.

I have enough behavior pinned down to write the port. I’m creating a small library with separate conversion and formatter modules, then a thin `/output/test17.rs` entrypoint that mirrors the original CLI and uses a C++-style 6-significant-digit printer instead of Rust’s default float formatting.

The first cut is in place. I’m compiling now and then diffing its stdout against the C++ executable on both the provided examples and a wider sample to catch any remaining formatting or sign mismatches.

item.text:
Created a Rust 2021 Cargo project in `/output` with the root entry file [test17.rs](/output/test17.rs), library wiring in [src/lib.rs](/output/src/lib.rs), conversion logic in [src/color.rs](/output/src/color.rs), and a C++-style float formatter in [src/formatter.rs](/output/src/formatter.rs). The executable is available at [test17](/output/test17), and `cargo build --release` also produced [target/release/test17](/output/target/release/test17).

The port matches the reference binary byte-for-byte, including CLI default behavior, partial-arg handling, negative zero cases, and `std::cout` default float formatting. Verification was done by comparing stdout against `/workspace/dataset/test17_executable` for the provided examples plus a 3,375-case grid sweep, with `DIFFS=0`.
